scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8877: Since a firewall change window this morning, BOTH pods
have lost access to every 10.200.0.x server: DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 time
out and no portal loads by name or by IP. Pod-to-pod traffic between
host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1 still works. Monitoring shows all OSPF
adjacencies Full and the 10.200.0.0/24 route present on every router.
Identify what is blocking the server farm.

injection.action: add a FORWARD DROP rule for all traffic destined to the server farm

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_3 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: router_core_3 is the mandatory transit for the server farm --
  switch_server_access attaches only to router_core_3 (172.16.0.10/31). The
  new rule `-A FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP` silently discards every
  FORWARDED packet destined to the farm, from both pods. Routing is
  genuinely healthy: OSPF hellos are INPUT/OUTPUT traffic on router_core_3
  (not FORWARD), so all adjacencies stay Full and 10.200.0.0/24 remains in
  every table -- the drop happens at the firewall layer after the routing
  decision. Pod-to-pod traffic transits router_core_1<->router_core_2 and
  matches no rule. Note: router_core_3's OWN pings to the farm still succeed
  (locally generated traffic traverses OUTPUT, not FORWARD) -- a useful
  discriminator.
Localization: router_core_3
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule for destination
  10.200.0.0/24 on router_core_3
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP` on router_core_3
scenario.fix_spec:
remove the DROP rule on router_core_3 --
`iptables -D FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP rule / firewall filter, not a routing fault
must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes that healthy OSPF plus present routes with silent forwarding loss indicates packet filtering on the transit path
bonus-notes-transit-choke: notes all farm traffic must transit router_core_3 (sole attachment of switch_server_access), which is why both pods are affected

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** An nftables FORWARD-chain drop rule injected into the kernel firewall of router_core_3 during the morning change window.

**Mechanism:** The rule `ip daddr 10.200.0.0/24 counter packets 24 bytes 2016 drop` sits in the `ip filter FORWARD` chain on router_core_3, the sole transit router between the core (router_core_1 / router_core_2) and the server-access segment (switch_server_access). The FORWARD hook fires on every packet that the router is forwarding — not packets it originates. Two classes of traffic are killed by a single rule: (1) pod-to-server requests (daddr = 10.200.0.x, dropped on the way in to the farm), and (2) server-to-pod replies (the reply packet carries the server's 10.200.0.x address as its *destination* on the return trip through router_core_3, so it is equally dropped). This bidirectional blackout perfectly explains why ICMP, DNS (UDP 53), and HTTP all fail while OSPF adjacencies and intra-subnet farm traffic remain healthy — OSPF control traffic is locally originated (not FORWARD-hooked), and farm-to-farm traffic never traverses router_core_3's FORWARD path.

**Localization:** router_core_3, `ip filter / FORWARD` chain, nftables. No other device carries a matching rule; infra_sweep flagged only this device out of 15 scanned.

**Root cause:** A blanket `ip daddr 10.200.0.0/24 drop` rule was erroneously applied to router_core_3's nftables FORWARD chain during the firewall change window, blocking all transit traffic to and from the server farm.

**Fix:** Remove the offending rule on router_core_3: `nft delete rule ip filter FORWARD handle <handle>` (retrieve the handle via `nft -a list chain ip filter FORWARD`), then verify pod-to-server ICMP and DNS restore to 0 % loss.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router_core_3 as the affected device multiple times (affected component, localization, and root cause).

per_axis.rationale: Fails because the writeup identifies an nftables FORWARD drop rule rather than the expected iptables FORWARD DROP rule on router_core_3 (firewall issue correctly identified but tooling mismatch).

per_axis.axis: must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes that healthy OSPF plus present routes with silent forwarding loss indicates packet filtering on the transit path
per_axis.rationale: True — the agent explicitly links healthy OSPF/full routes with silent packet loss on the FORWARD path, identifying a transit-path firewall/filter as the cause.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-transit-choke: notes all farm traffic must transit router_core_3 (sole attachment of switch_server_access), which is why both pods are affected
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router_core_3 is the sole transit between the core and switch_server_access, explaining why traffic from both pods is blocked.
Proposes removing the drop rule on router_core_3 (using nft delete rule with the rule handle), which matches the expected remediation to delete the blocking rule.

Investigation log explicitly shows host pings timing out, infra_sweep flagged router_core_3 with a matching drop rule, and nft list confirmed the FORWARD-chain drop with nonzero counters — so the diagnosis (remove that rule) is well supported. One mechanistic statement in the writeup (that server-to-pod replies carry 10.200.0.0/24 as their destination) is incorrect, though it doesn't change the core finding that forwarded packets to the farm are being dropped.
